chapters.title: Locked Eyes
chapters.html:
The air ran freely through his golden locks. The ground felt steady beneath his body. The tiny hands braiding his hair were lacking in gentleness, but gained in sweetness every time he heard the little girl laugh. 

Mydei sat there, a rare feeling of peacefulness filling him. He rarely had the time to simply enjoy the breeze and kids who loved to play with his hair, so he treasured this moment of freedom. Soon, he would be called back to attend another meeting. Later, he would be told to listen as dozens of men and women fought for his hand. Eventually, he would have to pick a spouse and accept the throne. 

But now. Now, tiny hands were making tiny braids in his hair. Small children were playing in circles around him. His mother would stall for him for as long as they could afford. So, Mydei treasured this moment, as it would pass all too soon. 

A few days ago, King Eurypon succumbed to illness. The kingdom mourned for seven days, before Queen Gorgo announced the Crown Prince Mydei’s ascension to King in two week's time. 

Before, there was the announcement of a banquet where young women and men could try for Mydeimos’s hand. It was less of a banquet and more of a tournament; anyone could join, but only the one who emerged victorious would be granted an audience with the Crown Prince. Then, Mydeimos could choose whether the winner was worthy of his hand. In his case, this meant a duel against him. It was unclear whether you had to win or simply hold your own against the Prince for him to choose you as his spouse. 

So began the chaos of hundreds, thousands of young adults arriving at Castrum Kremnos’s walls to take a shot at becoming the Crown Prince’s spouse. 

“Mydeimos,” His mother murmured, running her fingers through his hair. “I know you do not want to marry yet. But I am powerless to do anything, my son.” Her voice was regretful, genuine. “This is the tradition the Crown follows ever since our kingdom's foundation.”

Mydei knew. Of course, he knew. He was also aware it was not his mother's fault for being stripped of the choice when he would get married. It didn't mean he had to be happy about it. 

“I know.” He said simply. But he leaned into Gorgo’s touch. He loved his mother, and even if he was unhappy about this, he wouldn't take it out on her. 

“My dear Mydeimos.” She whispered, leaning down to press a gentle kiss to his forehead. She continued to run her fingers through Mydei's hair. “Do not feel pressured to accept someone you do not seem worthy. Of that, I will make sure you have the power.”

A small, gentle smile appeared on Mydei's face. “Thank you, mother.” His voice was quiet, appreciative. He knew his mother would do everything in her power to make sure Mydei had the most to say in the matter. 

They stayed like that the entire night, Mydei's head on his mother's lap, her fingers in his hair. They were always close, as his father had more expectations of him. Meanwhile his mother had none; she simply wished for him to be happy. 

And in that silent moment, there was no thought about his impending ascension on Mydei's mind. He was simply joyful to be in his mother's arms, cradled as though he was still nine years old and suffering through his worst case of an illness in years. They were simply Mydei and Gorgo, here. Not the Crown Prince and Queen of Castrum Kremnos. 

Mydei watched with a bored expression on his face as women and men fought each other. They were all so horribly weak. It would've made Mydei embarrassed if he was their teacher. Granted, it was only the beginning of the competition, and he saw a few good enough fighters, but they were unbearably rare. 

He refused the glass of wine he was offered. When he heard a chuckle, he looked up in slight annoyance that turned into surprise. 

“Ptolemy?” He questioned, straightening in his seat. 

“The one and only,” His friend grinned, sitting next to him. He offered him the glass once more with a clear amused smile. “Pomegranate juice. With milk.”

He blushed slightly in embarrassment, before taking the glass with a quiet grumble. Ptolemy laughed, before setting his cheek on his hand, leaning his elbow against the table. 

“Have you seen anyone who caught your eye yet?” He asked with clear curiosity, scanning the crowd and the ones currently dueling. 

“No.” Mydei responded drily, taking a sip of the juice. “Everyone is pathetic.”

Ptolemy laughed, shaking his head. “Not everyone is as good at fighting as you, you know?”

Mydei scowled. “Then they shouldn't even try. I won't pick anyone who isn't at the very least capable of holding their own against me.”

“So harsh,” Ptolemy sighed, wiping a fake tear. Mydei rolled his eyes at the dramatic action. 

They sat in companionable silence for the next few minutes, Mydei drinking his juice and Ptolemy watching the contestants curiously. At some point his gaze stopped at a corner of the room, looking intrigued. 

Mydei followed his friend's line of sight, only to see a duo of white and pink. 

A young man, with a bright smile was talking with his pink haired companion. The woman was staring back at the white haired man with a fond expression, dodging the other's hands which gesticulated wildly with practiced ease. Mydei found himself being strangely drawn to the man whose name he did not know. 

“Which one of them is here for the competition, do you think?” 

Mydei watched the pair some more. While the woman didn't seem to be particularly weak, she didn't look like a person who would wield a weapon. Meanwhile, the man had a sword strapped to his back. And while Mydei couldn't exactly see it all that well, he could tell it was a custom made weapon. 

“The man.” He said simply, his eyes never straying from the pair. 

The man was laughing now, his head thrown back because of something the woman had said. They looked like close friends; perhaps even siblings, though Mydei didn't know enough about them to make that assumption. It was strange; Mydei had no idea of the man's skill, and yet, for some reason, he couldn't wait to see him in the ring. 

His staring didn't go unnoticed by his friend, unfortunately, because when he next spoke his voice carried a teasing lilt. “Interested?”

Mydei huffed, not deeming that with a response. But for the rest of the night, his gaze kept returning to the man. 

It took an annoying amount of time for the only person Mydei was curious about to have his first fight. The moment he heard the words, “Next up, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae…” followed by the white haired man's entrance, Mydei's eyes immediately fixed on the duel. 

Phainon, huh? 

He felt strangely pleased to know the man's name. 

The moment the battle began, Mydei was convinced. 

Him. It's him. I want him.

Phainon's swordsmanship was mind-blowing. He moved gracefully, and yet Mydei had no doubts his strikes were deadly. He overpowered his opponent in mere seconds, going on offensive from the start. Mydei found himself entranced. Bewitched. Now that he was closer, he could appreciate Phainon's figure more. And, it was a good figure. He had thrown off his cloak before the match, so Mydei had full view of the man's muscles. He was undeniably handsome, his facial features pleasing to look at. 

The more Mydei watched, the more he was certain he wanted this man. He wanted Phainon to be his, to share vows with him and sit on the throne alongside him. 

If he wasn't so curious about how he would fare against him, for he had no doubt Phainon would win the competition, Mydei would announce the winner right after the end of Phainon's first battle.

Alas, he was too curious. So, he stayed quiet as Phainon successfully secured his first win, and resigned himself to waiting for the next few hours to stand against his future husband. 

Like Mydei predicted, Phainon had no issues in winning the competition. He was simply on a different level compared to other contestants. He was an actual warrior, which was exactly what Mydei was looking for. 

There was a break after Phainon was announced as the winner, for the man to rest before going against Mydei. Phainon looked genuinely shocked to have won, which amused Mydei. He didn't seem to have even entertained the idea of winning, which Mydei found strange. He was clearly the best of the contestants. His skill far exceeded the one who he fought in the final duel. 

During the break, Mydei slipped away to prepare for the following duel. He felt strangely excited about all this; he wondered how well the other would hold up against him and if, perhaps, Phainon would match his skill. 

He was alone in the room for a total of five minutes before he heard a knock, and then his mother came in. He raised an eyebrow at her, while she grinned. 

“I came to see how my son is feeling,” Gorgo walked closer to him, standing with her arms crossed, a knowing look in her eyes. 

Mydei couldn't help smiling. His mother truly knew him the best. “Excited.” He spoke honestly, for he had no reason to hide his feelings from her. “He's mine. I just want to duel him.”

Gorgo laughed, gathering his cheeks in her palms. “He seems to be a delightful young man.”

Mydei nodded absentmindedly, thinking back to Phainon waving his hands around like a madman. He also wanted to be as practiced at dodging him as his companion was. 

“What will you fight him with?” Gorgo asked curiously, looking around the room. “Your gauntlets, I assume?” She asked teasingly, not seeing any other weapons. 

Mydei nodded once more, “Phainon is strong. I want to see how he fares against me at my best.”

Gorgo looked as if she expected that response. “Well then. Remember to introduce me to my son-in-law when you have the time.”

He smiled, leaning slightly into her hands. “I will.”

They stayed like that for a couple more minutes, enjoying each other's presence, before Gorgo pulled away. 

“Don't hold back, Mydeimos.” 

Mydei grinned. “I don't plan on it.”

When Mydei was done preparing, he left the room with his gauntlets in place, and dressed in his usual fighting attire. For the banquet, he was required to wear something less revealing, which he found annoying. But now, standing inside of the ring, waiting for his future husband, Mydei felt as comfortable as he could get. 

The moment Mydei saw the crown of white hair, his attention snapped to him. There, Phainon stood looking terribly nervous and not at all confident like he was back during his final match. His companion was patting him on the back with a wide, teasing grin. Mydei managed to catch from the way her mouth moved three words, go get him.

At that, Phainon seemed to grow even more nervous, and Mydei felt amusement creep in. He wondered if perhaps he was goaded into this by that companion of his. If so, Mydei would have to thank her profusely.

Their eyes met, and Mydei could see Phainon stop breathing. To be honest, he might've also done so. Phainon's eyes were just… The most alluring shade of blue he had ever seen before. Mydei saw Phainon gulp, and traced the lines of his Adam's apple with his gaze. 

For a second, the world fell away and it was just the two of them holding each other's gaze. Then, Phainon gave him a small, but nervous smile, and Mydei's heart skipped a beat. 

Mydei hadn't even heard his voice yet, and he was already head over heels for him. Nikador give him strength.

He was the first to look away, though it took a great amount of strength. Mydei waited for Phainon to approach him, glancing only once to see his companion making excited hand gestures in his and Phainon's directions, before all but pushing the man to Mydei. 

When Phainon finally walked into the ring, and faced Mydei, the Prince took a while to take a proper look. Now that he was finally standing right in front of him, he could see all of Phainon's features clearer, and Mydei found he was even more handsome than he first thought. 

“Your Highness,” Phainon spoke, and Titan's above, his voice was amazing. “It's an honour to finally meet you.”

Now, if Mydei was capable of holding conversations, he would've graced that with a response just as polite. Instead, he hmphed. It was honestly fascinating to see someone turn this pale in a matter of seconds. It would've been more so if Mydei wasn't berating himself for further causing the other to be stressed out because of him. 

Phainon looked as though he wanted to be anywhere else but here. Which Mydei found a little offending, to be honest. It was his decision to enter the competition and end up winning. Why was he acting as though Mydei was threatening his life right now?

True, he isn't the greatest at social interaction, but surely not enough to make his future husband scared for his life? 

Oh, fuck this, he was definitely scaring his future husband. 

“Mydei.” He said, stretching his arms. 

Phainon blinked, forgetting his dawning fear for a couple of seconds. “What?”

“Mydei.” He repeated. For further clarification, he stated, “My name.”

Phainon did not look as though he found the clarification useful. “Your name.”

Mydei hmphed.

“I am aware of your name, Your Highness.” Phainon said slowly, as though Mydei was a child. 

Mydei felt annoyed. “Don't call me that.”

Meanwhile, Phainon was even more confused, it seemed. “What?”

Mydei held back a groan. Maybe Phainon was not as perfect as he imagined. It's too bad he already found himself loving him. 

“Call me Mydei.” That had to be obvious enough, even for someone as dense as Phainon, it would seem. 

Unfortunately, that confused Phainon even more. “Huh?”

Oh, Nikador help him.

“Are you acting or are you genuinely this stupid?” Mydei snapped, crossing his arms with a scowl. His future husband couldn't be this dumb, could he?

Phainon looked torn between being offended and scared of angering Mydei. Which was a little annoying, as Mydei would prefer the man speaking his mind with him. But that would come with time, he would make sure of that. 

“Apologies for my behaviour, Your—” He paused, seeing Mydei glare at him. He continued slowly, as though he was waiting for a vicious beast to jump him. “Mydei.”

“Accepted.” Mydei waved a hand, before uncrossing his arms. “Shall we duel?”

Phainon perked up slightly, though his head tilted sideways in confusion when he saw Mydei without a weapon. “Ah, your weapon, Mydei?”

He shrugged, settling into a fighting stance. “Don't need one.”

Phainon blinked, before looking down at his sword. “Should I refrain from using mine, then?”

Mydei scowled again. There's no way. He wanted to fight Phainon to see his real abilities, and the man was clearly a swordsman. He wanted Phainon to fight him with all he had. 

“No need.” 

The other looked lost for a few seconds, before shrugging it off and copying Mydei. “All right then, Mydei.” Here, he gave him a confident smile, or what was an attempt at one. “I won't go easy on you.”

Mydei smirked. “Me neither.”

And then they were off. 

Immediately upon contact, Mydei noted gleefully that Phainon's strikes were indeed strong. Mydei could actually feel the man's strength coursing through his body. The only time Mydei felt challenged by someone was when he fought his parents and teacher. And now, Phainon. 

The man was actually keeping up with him. Better, he was quickly becoming an equal match for Mydei. This was so much more than he was hoping for. To find out the man he found himself so intrigued in, was his equal… 

Phainon was his.

Their duel went on, and on, and on. At this point Mydei was fighting purely because he enjoyed it. Meeting Phainon's strikes with his gauntlets was exhilarating. The power behind those strikes was immense, and the only reason Mydei's arms were still intact was the fact he was simply used to taking such heavy hits from his father, and learned how to do it safely. 

He could tell Phainon was also enjoying this, based off of his grin. Their eyes were locked for most of the duel, simply enjoying fighting someone capable of challenging them. 

Eventually, the fight dragged on for so long, with no real victor, that his mother intervened. She clapped two times, and the room instantly became quiet. Mydei took Phainon's blade in his hand as it came down, knowing he might've not heard his mother. 

“I think that is quite enough.” Gorgo spoke normally, yet her voice carried even to the furthest corners of the room. “Mydeimos, now is the time you tell us your choice.”

Mydei nodded silently, before turning back to Phainon. The other was breathing heavily, but that was about the same as Mydei. The two locked eyes once more. Mydei could see Phainon becoming more nervous the longer he stayed quiet, so he took pity on his future husband. 

“Phainon of Aedes Elysiae,” He hid a grin when he noticed Phainon shivering upon Mydei saying his name. “Will be my husband.”

Cheers erupted from everyone around. He heard his mother briefly say, “very well”, before his attention was back on Phainon. Who looked downright befuddled at the news. He looked like a very confused chimera, and it only made Mydei love him more. 

Mydei still held Phainon's blade in his hand, but the other seemed to have forgotten about it. Mydei was certain that if he were to take his weapon now, Phainon would not even blink twice. Once more, Mydei took pity on him, and closed the distance between them, making sure not to let go of the sword since he wasn't confident the other wouldn't just drop it. 

“You look as though someone just kicked you in the gut.” He said drily. 

Phainon seemed to finally snap out of his dazed state, though he still looked shocked. “You… What?”

Mydei rolled his eyes. “Is ‘what’ your favourite word? You use it a concerning amount.”

Phainon rolled his eyes, tugging back his sword. “I think it's completely justifiable to be shocked when you're announced as someone's husband-to-be.”

Mydei raised an unimpressed eyebrow. “Shouldn't you have entertained the thought considering you entered a competition meant to reveal a person worthy of being my spouse?”

The other groaned, his cheeks going slightly pink. Cute.

“Cyrene never said what it was for! She just said it was a competition where I had the chance to fight Castrum Kremnos's Crown Prince! Of course I'd accept!”

Mydei snorted in amusement. He was right about Cyrene, his companion he assumed, dragging Phainon here. 

“Did you not hear anything in the city? Or from other contestants?”

Phainon huffed, looking away to attempt to hide his embarrassed expression. He was not successful. 

“We showed up late so we weren't in the city for long, and the other contestants around me didn't say anything until I was well into my fifth duel.” He sounded like a petulant child at that moment. Mydei had no idea why he found that so adorable.

“Well,” Mydei dragged with a smirk. “You unknowingly captured my attention ever since your first fight. This was all just for my own entertainment.”

Phainon turned to him with an open mouth. “What.”

He snorted, his grin widening. “You were my future husband from the beginning. I just wanted to see how well you could do against me. And I have to say, I'm pleased to find out you're my equal.”

Phainon flushed, scrambling for a response. “That's— You're ridiculous.”

Mydei just shrugged.

Later, he would drag off Phainon to meet his mother. She would shower the other with praises about his swordsmanship and request him to teach young warriors what he knew. 

Later, Phainon would introduce him to Cyrene, his closest friend who was like his sister. Mydei would thank her for making Phainon attend the competition, to which she would laugh and embrace Mydei like she would a brother. 

Much later, Mydei and Phainon would sit on Mydei's balcony, and talk about their lives. Mydei would learn about Phainon losing his family, Cyrene being the only one he had left. And Mydei would tell Phainon about how despite not being close to his father, his death still affected him, and for the first few days he couldn't leave his mother's room, in fear of her also succumbing to illness. 

And later, they would share their first kiss under the moonlight, brought together by a competition neither of them wanted. But it became the moment their paths met, and they would cherish it until their last breaths.

“Mydei,” His husband spoke, running his fingers through Mydei's hair. “What if I mess up at ruling the kingdom with you?” Phainon's voice was full of worry and doubt. “I'm not a royal, hell, not even a noble. I have no idea how this works. 

Mydei looked up at him, and put a hand on Phainon's cheek. “You won't mess up.” He said so with a certainty that resembled his confidence in battle. “And even if you do, I'll be right there with you.”

Phainon sighed, a soft smile appearing on his lips. He leaned down to press a gentle kiss to Mydei's temple. “You sound so confident.”

“Because I am.” 

Phainon snorted, pulling away. “Of course. How could I doubt Mydeimos, the Undying?”

Mydei blushed at that, and pushed his face further away. “Shut up! I told you to not call me that!”

The other grinned, “But why? That's your title, is it not?”

“Not for you.” Mydei huffed, looking away.

“Not for me?”

With a deep breath, Mydei looked back at Phainon and spoke with rare nervousness. “For you, I'm not the King of Castrum Kremnos. Or Mydeimos the Undying.” He paused, and despite his cheeks warming up, he continued. “For you, I'm just Mydei.”

Phainon was speechless for a few seconds, before chuckling softly and staring back at Mydei with fondness. “Alright, just Mydei.” 

Their eyes locked for some time, content just to look at each other. 

The moment was broken when Phainon said with a teasing lilt, “So, is that why you wanted me to drop the ‘Your Highness’ back then?”

“I'll throw you off the balcony.”

“Shutting up now.”

Mydei sat leaning against a tree. Tiny hands were braiding his hair. A weight was settled on his lap, and his fingers were burrowed in white hair. 

Gentle wind caressed his hair and cheeks. Children ran around him and Phainon in circles. 

He was at peace. And this time, he could truly relax, without needing to savour the moment. For he knew many more moments like this were to come.
